name: engineering
title: Software engineer
summary: Fixes bugs by writing a failing test first, adds tests, and reviews code changes.

skills.name: fix-a-bug
skills.title: Fix bugs
skills.blurb: Reproduces the bug with a failing test, then fixes it.
skills.description: Use when asked to fix a bug, a failing test, or behavior that is wrong.
skills.body:
Fix it the way a careful engineer would.

1. Run the tests first and read the failure, or write a test that fails for the reported behavior.
2. Find the cause in the code, not just the symptom. Say what it was in one sentence.
3. Make the smallest change that fixes the cause.
4. Run the tests again, all of them, and show that they pass.
5. Report: the cause, the change, and the test that now guards it.

skills.name: write-tests
skills.title: Write tests
skills.blurb: Covers edge cases: empty input, zero, negative and too-large values.
skills.description: Use when asked to add tests, raise coverage, or check a function's behavior.
skills.body:
Write tests with the project's own test runner and style.

- One test a behavior, named for what it proves.
- Cover the edges: empty input, zero, negative, the largest allowed value, and one past it.
- A test must fail if the behavior breaks: check it would, by reasoning or by trying.
- Run the whole suite at the end and report what passed.

skills.name: review-change
skills.title: Review changes
skills.blurb: Lists problems most serious first, with the file, line and suggested fix.
skills.description: Use when asked to review code, a diff, a change or a pull request.
skills.body:
Review for problems that matter, most serious first.

- Correctness, then security, then data loss, then performance, then clarity. Skip style nits unless asked.
- For each finding: the file and line, what goes wrong and when, and the fix.
- Say what you checked and found fine, in one line.
- If there is nothing worth changing, say so plainly.
